searchText: <@!243183686562873344> how long did it take you to sync frontier? I never timed it, but I guess like 4 hours. cpython or pypy? pypy Hm. HMMMM... I had block 389315 take 25 seconds And the whole thing is taking way more hours than it should. Time to debug. Are there docs on how to do what you guys are doing, syncing the chain with the pyspec? No, just the tool itself: ``` ethereum-spec-sync --help ``` After installing I should add a note to the README can anyone give me an example of how to use `--rpc-url` HTTP only? IPC supported? `INFO:ethereum_spec_tools.sync:block 389315 applied (took 0.16856276299995443s)` on pypy on my machine. Took about half an hour to sync there from genesis. (forgive me for not just digging into the code...., I know...) `ethereum-spec-sync --rpc-url=http://127.0.0.1:8545/ --optimized --persist ~/.block-db` for example. In principle you should be able to use an Infura endpoint, but you will probably get rate limited/billed a lot. I suspect it's the RLP decoding. Haven't confirmed though. Something that you guys *might* look at is doing "beam sync" style block execution with an archive node backing the state data. This would allow you to do concurrent block execution as well as just dropping into the chain at arbitrary points. It would add complexity to the state management aspect of things but if you really want to be able to validate all the way to the front of the chain in a reasonable amount of time.... I think you guys are gonna end up needing to be able to execute blocks in parallel, otherwise your sync times as the gas limits get higher and the total state size gets larger are going to grow and grow and grow....
